subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated executions of the same command with the same nonzero exit identity count as no progress even when their output text changes?
rationale: Tests and live proof establish that the implementation works, but they cannot choose the product-level availability tradeoff between stopping runaway retries and allowing commands whose nonzero output changes meaningfully across attempts.

options.title: Accept stable failure identity
options.body: Treat matching structured nonzero outcomes as no progress, rebase the branch, refresh the focused proof, and merge.

options.title: Preserve semantic output distinctions
options.body: Revise the fingerprint to retain a deliberately normalized semantic output component, accepting that volatile text may still let some loops evade detection.

options.title: Keep current output-sensitive behavior
options.body: Do not merge this heuristic and leave the canonical issue open while a different loop-control policy is designed.

recommendation.title: Accept stable failure identity
recommendation.body: Treat matching structured nonzero outcomes as no progress, rebase the branch, refresh the focused proof, and merge.
